science.headline:
How Hormone Therapy
Differs From Supplements
science.body: Hormones are chemical messengers that help regulate many body functions, and levels can change with age. When lab results and symptoms point to a deficiency, a licensed clinician may consider hormone therapy. Some hormone preparations used here are compounded and are not FDA-approved. Results vary.
bullets: Prescribed by real licensed medical doctors
Regular lab monitoring as determined by your provider

cards.title: Bio-Identical Options
cards.detail: Bio-identical hormones have the same molecular structure as hormones your body makes. Some are FDA-approved products and some are compounded, and compounded products are not FDA-approved.

myths.reality: No. Bio-identical hormones have the same molecular structure as the hormones your body makes. Your provider sets a dose based on your labs and monitors your levels over time.

myths.myth: Do I have to stay on this forever?
myths.reality: Duration depends on your diagnosis and clinical goals. Hormone therapy is often long-term, and your provider will review the plan with you, including what to expect if you stop.

Hormone therapy is prescribed by a licensed clinician after an evaluation and monitored with regular lab checks. All hormone therapies carry risks, which your provider will discuss with you. Compounded medications are not FDA-approved, and the FDA does not review them for safety, effectiveness, or quality.

faqs.question: Do I need a doctor's prescription for hormone therapy?
faqs.answer: Yes. All hormone optimization treatments are prescription medications. You will consult with our licensed medical doctor who reviews your health history and bloodwork before prescribing a custom plan tailored to your body.

faqs.question: What does the doctor-guided hormone program include?
faqs.answer: Your program includes direct consultations with our board-certified medical doctor, full baseline and follow-up blood tests, custom hormone preparations (some are compounded and are not FDA-approved), and ongoing medical check-ins.

faqs.question: How fast will I feel results from hormone therapy?
faqs.answer: Timelines vary by person, hormone and dose. Your provider will monitor your symptoms and labs and adjust your plan. Results vary and are not guaranteed.

faqs.question: Is hormone therapy appropriate for both men and women?
faqs.answer: Hormone therapy is prescribed for men and women when symptoms and lab results support it, and the treatment differs for each. Every hormone therapy has risks and is not right for everyone. Your provider will review your history and risks with you and monitor your labs during treatment.

faqs.question: What side effects are possible, and is this the same as using steroids?
faqs.answer: Hormone therapy prescribed by a clinician is not the same as anabolic steroid use. Side effects are possible with any hormone therapy and depend on the hormone, the dose and your health. Your provider will explain the risks, calibrate your dose to your lab results and monitor you with regular check-ins and lab work.

faqs.question: How do I get started with hormone optimization?
faqs.answer: Getting started is simple! Call our clinic today at (727) 476-8966 or click 'Book Your Doctor Consultation' online. Our doctor will order a quick blood test, review your results, and launch your personalized vitality plan.

faqs.question: Are compounded hormones FDA-approved?
faqs.answer: Some hormone therapies are FDA-approved products, and some are compounded. Compounded medications are not FDA-approved. The FDA does not review compounded medications for safety, effectiveness, or quality before they are marketed. These products are prepared by a licensed pharmacy for individual patients when a licensed clinician determines that an FDA-approved product does not meet that patient’s specific clinical needs. Your provider will explain which option is being prescribed and the risks of each.
